# Isle of Skye

With rugged mountains, sweeping coastal views, rich clan history and unforgettable wildlife experiences, the ‘Misty Isle’ is sure to captivate you.

## The Isle of Skye at a glance

- Food & drink:
Fresh seafood, whisky, venison, fine dining, honesty boxes

- History & heritage:
Armadale Castle, Dunvegan Castle, Gaelic, clearance villages, brochs, Museum of Island Life

- Nature & outdoors:
Isle of Raasay, Sleat Peninsula, dramatic mountains, sea cliffs, sandy beaches, hiking, sea kayaking, white‑tailed eagles

- Towns & villages:
Armadale, Broadford, Carbost, Dunvegan, Elgol, Glendale, Kyleakin, Portree, Staffin, Uig


Map of Scotland

## What to expect on the Isle of Skye

Journey across the sea to Skye, an island off Scotland’s north-west coast shaped by history, Gaelic culture, folklore and volcanic landscapes. Watch sunlight touch the Old Man of Storr, trace dinosaur footprints, explore ancient castles, spot marine wildlife and browse local galleries. From the Cuillin to neighbouring Raasay, Skye invites you to slow down and experience a different side of Scotland.

## Highlights on the Isle of Skye

Skye is made for exploring. Whether you want to unwind in its natural landscapes, discover local arts and culture, or savour the island’s food and drink, there are experiences to suit every pace and interest throughout the year.

### Dramatic landscapes and experiences

Skye’s windswept landscapes leave a lasting impression. Explore glens, coastlines and mountains shaped over millions of years. From gentle low-level walks to challenging mountain climbs, there’s an option for every ability. Looking for something more adventurous? Navigate Skye’s coastline by kayak, cycle past ancient landslides on an e-bike or see Skye from the water on a high-speed RIB. Afterwards, take a refreshing dive in the sea before warming up in one of the island’s sea saunas.

[Discover more activities on Skye](https://visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2026/09/28/quiraing-isle-of-skye.jpg)

Quiraing, Isle of Skye

### Sample local food and drink

Skye is a foodie paradise. From freshly landed langoustines, lobster, mussels and oysters to dishes made with local venison and lamb, the island’s restaurants serve the best from land and sea. You will also find creative vegetarian and vegan dishes showcasing seasonal produce from Skye and beyond as well as Michelin star restaurant, Loch Bay. Start the day with a coffee at Birch in Portree and pick up some freshly home baked delights from bakeries or honesty boxes. No visit to Skye is complete without a taste of two of its finest whiskies. Slàinte!

[Find your favourite dish on Skye](https://https//visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/a-foodie's-guide/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/09/06/the-oyster-shed)

Mussels from The Oyster Shed

© Kim Walton

### Get inspired by arts and crafts

The landscapes of Skye have long inspired artists and makers. Discover galleries and studios dotted around the island, where contemporary ceramics, paintings, textiles and traditional crafts reflect the colours, stories and beautiful nature of Skye. Use the Art Skye Map to visit local artists such as [Skyeskyns](https://www.skyeskyns.co.uk/), tanners, makers and suppliers of luxurious sheepskins, home accessories and sustainably-made clothing.

[View the Art Skye Map](https://www.art-skye.co.uk/art-skye-map/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/01/25/edinbane-pottery)

Edinbane Pottery, Isle of Skye

© Edinbane Pottery

### Delve into the history and heritage of the island

Skye’s human history stretches back thousands of years, from prehistoric beginnings and Iron Age settlements to powerful clan rivalries a few centuries ago. Explore the remains of ancient brochs, discover how islanders once lived at the Skye Museum of Island Life, and uncover the stories of the two main clans of the island at Dunvegan Castle and Armadale Castle. Walk through remote glens where the remains of villages lie scattered across the landscape, a poignant reminder of the communities who once called Skye home.

[Discover the fascinating history of Skye](https://https//visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/local-culture-and-history/)

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/09/14/museum-of-island-life-skye)

Skye Museum of Island Life

## What's on in Skye

From the unforgettable atmosphere of Skye Live music festival to traditional tunes in small halls and the Highland games, find your next event on the Isle of Skye.

previousnext

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/07/20/skye-road-bridge)

### [Skye Live Festival](https://www.skyelive.co.uk/)

Enjoy traditional and contemporary music at this yearly festival in Portree.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2022/11/29/highland-dancers-at-the-ballater-highland-games)

### [Skye Highland Games](https://www.skye-highland-games.co.uk/)

Experience the Highland Games this August.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2024/01/12/whisky-glass.jpg)

### [Hebridean Whisky Festival](https://hebrideanwhisky.com/festival/)

Celebrate island whisky with tastings, distillery experiences, masterclasses, live music and local culture across the Hebrides.

![](https://www.visitscotland.com/binaries/content/gallery/visitscotland/cms-images/2023/01/25/portree)

### [SEALL Festival of Small Halls Festival](https://www.seall.co.uk/festival-of-small-halls/)

8 artists will spend time sharing music, ideas and influences before creating a series of entirely unique sets especially for the festival.

## See the Isle of Skye through a new lens

Meet the Old Man of Storr and follow in the footsteps of dinosaurs. Roam through some of the world's most recognisable scenery and charge up your batteries with local seafood and a dram.

## Discover your ideal location on the Isle of Skye

With several peninsulas spreading out like wings from the centre to the sea, it’s no wonder that Skye is often referred to as the “winged isle”. Discover what makes each part of the island so unique and choose your ideal base for your holiday.

### Portree

With its brightly coloured harbour and sheltered bay, Portree is a great place to experience island life. Browse the independent shops, and watch fishing boats come and go in the harbour. In the evening, visit one of the local restaurants or pubs and enjoy fresh seafood, live music and views across the bay. With good transport links and its central location, Portree is an ideal base for exploring the rest of the island.

[Visit Portree](https://visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/portree/)

### Trotternish

Head north of Portree to explore a landscape shaped over millions of years. Discover dinosaur footprints at An Corran beach and Brother’s Point, walk up to meet the Old Man of Storr, see the waters of Mealt Falls tumble into the sea beside Kilt Rock, and take in the sweeping views across the Quiraing. Visit the haunted ruins of Duntulm Castle, perched high on the cliffs, and stop in Staffin or Uig, the peninsula’s two main villages, for some delicious food.

[Discover Staffin in Trotternish](https://www.isleofskye.com/staffin)

### Dunvegan & Waternish

Discover the history and creativity of north-west Skye in Dunvegan and Waternish. Explore Dunvegan Castle, the ancestral seat of Clan MacLeod for more than 800 years, then follow the coastal road to Coral Beach where light sands and turquoise waters create a striking contrast in the landscape. Continue to Waternish where studios and galleries are filled with the work of local artists. Browse handmade ceramics, textiles and artwork inspired by the islands’ landscapes, and enjoy stunning views across the water to the Outer Hebrides.

[Discover Dunvegan](https://visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/dunvegan/)

[Explore Waternish](https://www.visit-waternish.co.uk/)

### Duirinish

Duirinish is the westernmost peninsula of the island. Discover Skye’s weaving traditions at Skye Weavers and try your hand at pedalling the loom to create tweed. Continue to Neist Point, to the far west of the island, for stunning views and the chance to see dolphins, whales or even orcas before finishing the day with some fine dining at The Three Chimneys, one of Skye’s best-known restaurants.

[Explore the Duirinish peninsula](https://www.isleofskye.com/glendale)

### Minginish

Explore the Minginish peninsula in the south-west, home to the famous Fairy Pools, the Black Cuillin and Talisker Distillery. Dip your toe in the crystal-clear water beneath cascading waterfalls, stroll along the volcanic sands of Glenbrittle Beach, and take in the view of Skye’s towering mountain peaks. Stop for lunch at Café Cùil or sample freshly caught seafood at the Oyster Shed before visiting Talisker Distillery. End the day at The Old Inn in Carbost where live music and a welcoming atmosphere give you a taste of island life.

[Explore Carbost and the Minginish peninsula](https://www.isleofskye.com/carbost)

### Broadford & Strathaird

Broadford is Skye’s second-largest town and a popular base for exploring the island with views across Broadford Bay and plenty of places to eat, drink and stay. As you travel south towards Elgol, you can see traces of Skye’s industrial past at the Skye Marble Line. In Elgol, you can enjoy sweeping views of the Cuillin mountain range before taking a boat trip to the remote Loch Coruisk. Or head out to sea in the summer months in search of puffins and other seabirds around the Small Isles, including Canna.

[Plan your trip to Broadford](https://visitwesthighlands.co.uk/travel-guides/skye-raasay-and-lochalsh/broadford/)

[Visit the village of Elgol](https://www.isleofskye.com/elgol-torrin)

### Sleat

Known as the “Garden of Skye”, the Sleat peninsula in the south offers a gentler side of the island, with woodland trails, sheltered coastlines and tranquil gardens. Visit Torabhaig Distillery to discover Skye’s whisky-making traditions, explore history at Armadale Castle or enjoy woodland walks with views to the Sound of Sleat. Finish your day with a dining experience at Kinloch Lodge or Duisdale House and watch ferries cross the water towards Mallaig on the mainland.

[Visit Sleat, the Garden of Skye](https://www.sleatperfectlyskye.com/)

### Getting to the Isle of Skye

Ferry

## Ferry

The CalMac ferry (Mallaig to Skye) runs daily from the port of Mallaig in the west Highlands to Armadale in Sleat on the south of Skye. You can get to Mallaig by road or train. Booking in advance is strongly advised, especially for travel in the summer months.

The privately-operated seasonal Glenelg ferry connects Glenelg on the mainland with Kylerhea on Skye. Please note, there are no bus services for this connection.

[Find out more about the ferry to Skye](https://www.calmac.co.uk/en-gb/destinations/skye/)

* * *

Train

## Train

A train service connects Inverness with Kyle of Lochalsh, the last town on the mainland before the Skye Bridge. From Kyle of Lochalsh, you can travel by bus onto the island.

[Find trains to Kyle of Lochalsh](https://www.nationalrail.co.uk/destinations/trains-to-kyle-of-lochalsh/)

* * *

Bus and coach

## Bus and coach

Long distance coach services including Citylink and Ember operate from Inverness, Edinburgh and Glasgow to the main villages along the A87 on the island. Bus fares for adults are now capped at no more than £2.

- Bus from Edinburgh to Portree: 7 hours 30 minutes
- Bus from Glasgow to Portree: 6 hours 30 minutes
- Bus from Inverness to Portree: 3 hours and 30 minutes

Find out more on the bus to Skye with [Citylink](https://www.citylink.co.uk/get-inspired/destinations/isle-of-skye/) or [Ember](https://www.ember.to/)

* * *

Driving

## Driving

Skye is well connected to the rest of Scotland by road and ferry.

- Car from Edinburgh to Portree: 5 hours 30 minutes
- Car from Glasgow to Portree: 5 hours
- Car from Inverness to Portree: 3 hours

Driving around Skye is the preferred option for many visitors as it offers the most flexibility and access to more remote spots. However, it is good to remember that some of the island's roads are single track, with ample passing places.

[Read more about driving in Scotland](https://www.visitscotland.com/travel-planning/driving)

[See all available travel options for the Isle of Skye](https://www.isleofskye.com/skye-guide/travel-tips)

* * *

### Accessibility

Everyone is welcome on Skye. Some areas on the island are rugged in nature, but many attractions, accommodations and restaurants are accessible. For more information on wheelchair-friendly walks, accessible parking and local facilities, see the website of [Skye for All](http://skyeforall.co.uk/walks-on-skye/).

Read disabled access reviews of tourism venues in Scotland, all written by disabled people and their friends and families.

## FAQs

When is the best time to visit the Isle of Skye?

### When is the best time to visit the Isle of Skye?

May to September is a great, though potentially busy, time to visit Skye, with longer days meaning there is more time to explore the island's dramatic landscapes and picturesque villages, though you can enjoy the island all year round.

Spring (March–May): Head to the Fairy Glen as wildflowers begin to bloom, adding fresh colour to one of Skye's most magical landscapes.

Summer (June–August): Long daylight hours are perfect for exploring iconic sights such as the Old Man of Storr.

Autumn (September–November–): Enjoy quieter walks through the Quiraing and around the Trotternish Peninsula, where golden and russet hues add extra colour to Skye's dramatic scenery.

Winter (December–February): Experience a wilder side of Skye, with peaceful roads, moody landscapes and cosy evenings in Portree after a day of sightseeing.

* * *

How long should I stay on Skye?

### How long should I stay on Skye?

We recommend spending at least 3–5 days to experience the island fully. This gives you time to explore the stunning landscape, discover historic sites, experience island culture, take a boat trip, and enjoy some of the best walking routes you have ever encountered.

* * *

Where can I stay on Skye?

### Where can I stay on Skye?

It depends on your own preference but there are a few things to consider. Skye is a big island and public transport is limited. If you’re using public transport, Portree is the main town on the island and has good links to Dunvegan, Uig, Staffin and Broadford.

Choose from a variety of places to stay, from campsites and hostels to hotels and B&Bs. Remember to book your accommodation in advance, especially during the summer months.

[Find your accommodation with IsleofSkye.com](https://www.isleofskye.com/accommodation)
